summary:
“Green. Buddy, can you hear me?” He carefully cupped the side of Green’s face and turned his head towards him. “Just hang in there, okay? You’ll be alright, you’re–”
Kai froze.
He doubted he would have been able to recognize that face sooner, blinded as he’d been by worry over Green’s state to pay much attention to what he looked like beneath the mask. But now, with all his focus trained on the blonde boy – someone who should have been a stranger – it was undeniable to Kai whose face he was looking at. Who it was wearing Green’s ninja gi, lying in the middle of the broken remains of Green’s mech. Who it was Kai had been so afraid for, just a moment ago, but now only engendered in him a cold white shock.
“Lloyd… Garmadon…?”

summary: And the first time he saw her as a daughter.Ever since unlocking her True Potential, Sora has had to come to terms with the fact that her parents were just awful people. They never loved her, only the family image they gained from having her. That was fine though. It wasn’t like Sora needed parents, even if the idea of having someone be there for you and care for you in that sort of way had always appealed to her. Besides, if her own parents couldn’t give her that, who else could? Why bother hoping for something you’ll never have?Ever since stopping the Mergequakes, Lloyd has come to realize just how much he cares for his students, and how afraid he is of losing them. All he wants is to protect them and keep them close. However, he knows it can’t last forever. Arin’s parents are still out there somewhere, and Sora… well, she’s independent, and he wouldn’t want to be the one to tie her down. Besides, it’s not as if they see him as anything more than their teacher and friend. Why try and change something that’s not broken?Sora never asked to be chosen. Lloyd never thought she wanted to be. Turns out family can form even when neither one is aware of it. Funny how love works like that.

“So, the mural was real?” Cole asked as they walked down the hall.
“I did say that doctor was full of shit,” Morro reminded them.
“History is art,” Zane said. “Not science. Even an expert such as Dr. Saunders can be mistaken from time to time.”
Morro gave him a disbelieving look. “It was only forty years ago, Zane. People are still alive from then. It is not hard to ask a simple question of those that were there.”
“That guy rubs my skin the wrong way,” Kai told them. The man had made him uncomfortable since they met.
“Same,” Morro agreed.
“He’s just a historian,” Zane pointed out. “What could he have done to spark distrust?”
Kai rubbed the head of the snake. “Just a feeling, Zane.”
“Hmm. Might serve to investigate that.”

summary: "En las sombras de Ninjago, la paz siempre fue una mentira."El Maestro Wu, atormentado por un pasado sangriento y una promesa que no pudo entender, reúne a un grupo de jóvenes marcados no por el destino, sino por la tragedia. Sobrevivientes de la esclavitud, el abandono, el abuso y la traición más visceral, han encontrado en él un mentor y entre ellos, un refugio.Kai, Nya, Jay, Cole y Zane no son héroes de leyenda; son almas rotas que aprendieron a pelear con las cicatrices que el mundo les dejó. Pero cuando una amenaza antigua resurge, dejando su siniestro emblema —una serpiente enroscada en un ojo— en cada crimen, se darán cuenta de que sus dolorosos pasados no eran casualidad.En el corazón de la conspiración yace un secreto: un fantasma del pasado, una clave viviente cuya existencia hará que todo lo que creían saber sobre su dolor se desmorone. ¿Quién es el prisionero sin nombre que podría ser la salvación o la perdición de todos?Para enfrentar la oscuridad que se avecina, deberán aceptar que su mayor fuerza no yace en su poder, sino en el dolor que los une. El precio de la victoria podría ser aceptar que son, y siempre serán, hijos del dolor.

The Bounty-II was supposed to be simple: a seven-day Rite mission serving as the final test for the next generation of space protectors. For cadets raised within the Program since childhood, it was more than training—it was tradition, expectation, and the future they had been shaped for their entire lives.
But when the ship drifts into a sector tied to sealed reports and long-buried incidents, the mission begins to unravel.
An unknown infection spreads quietly through the systems and crew alike, twisting technology, behavior, and trust into something unrecognizable. As communications fail and paranoia takes hold, Cole, Jay, Kai, Nya, Lloyd, Zane, and Pixal are forced into impossible choices: who can be trusted, what risks are worth taking, and how far loyalty can stretch before it becomes dangerous.
Every action carries consequences. Every hesitation matters. And aboard a ship built on decades of sacrifice and carefully hidden truths, survival quickly becomes more than staying alive.
Because some things in space don’t die quietly.
And some mistakes were never truly left behind.

“(Y/n)?”
A call of your name had you turning to your right and suddenly, you were frozen like the ice you created. Is that…?
How did the monkey king know your name? Then another surprise hit you when the monkey king began smiling, one you would give to someone who is dearly close to you. The monkey king then began rambling.
“I thought I had lost you forever!” You felt the hug getting tighter and a deep feeling in you is telling you that he isn’t done with his ramblings, so before he could say another word. You let out your words that you had wanted to say the first second the monkey king had hugged you.

Ao Bing is gone. But the Spirit Pearl says otherwise.
Grief-scarred and hollowed by loss, Ne Zha descends into Diyu to return the half of Ao Bing’s soul he’s unknowingly carried ever since that night—drawn by a blue flicker in his own eyes and a presence that refuses to fade. He meant only to give Ao Bing peace.
He did not mean to accidentally reform the Spirit Pearl in his hands.
And when the Pearl stabilizes, Heaven panics, Wukong swears, and Ne Zha walks out of the underworld with no explanation and a glowing relic in his pocket.
It isn’t until several days later—when the Spirit Pearl’s shell fully mends—that something stirs. A tiny loong spirit curls out of the reformed light and onto Ne Zha’s shoulder, silent and unsure, but unmistakably Ao Bing.
Heaven calls Ne Zha’s actions rebellion.Wukong calls it dangerous.The mortal realm calls it an omen.
Ne Zha calls it love.
And he would tear through every realm again if it meant Ao Bing could finally rest—or finally return.

summary: Before Clouse became Chen’s right-hand sorcerer, there was Arabella—a prodigious dark arts student who manipulated illusions. Like Clouse, she was groomed by Master Chen for manipulation, deceit, and power, but her ambition was always her own. Using forbidden spells, Arabella kept her body young while her soul aged with every cruel deed she committed. Despite her cold loyalty to Chen, she once shared a volatile and secretive rivalry with Garmadon—a relationship born of mutual contempt, obsession, and darkness. When Garmadon began to fall to the Great Devourer's venom and his power turned destructive, Arabella was the only one who could match his raw force in battle. Something twisted always lingered between them: lust, hatred, and the terrifying understanding that they saw themselves in each other. But Garmadon left it all behind to pursue a new path. He married Misako and tried to tame the storm inside.Now, years later, during the Tournament of Elements, Arabella is still at Chen’s side. Her appearance rattles Garmadon, who has joined the tournament to guide Lloyd and the Ninja. As the tournament progresses, so does the reawakening of Garmadon’s shadowed instincts—and the dark bond he once shared with Arabella.

There’s something wrong with Jay.

Wojira is rising.

summary:
That sent them deep in thought, bringing a heavy, contemplative silence with it, but thankfully, Bolobo was able to make them see how damaging everything was. It was quiet for a moment until Jay, the most vocal about his fear, got up and walked over to his little brother. Lloyd didn’t have time to say anything until Jay dropped to his knees and hugged him.
 
Immediately, he was transported to a time when he was still young and annoying. An angry kid who was too cute to really be threatening. He was hugged like a child, arms wrapped carefully around his head as if to comfort him from another nightmare about fighting his father. Lloyd let out a breath he didn’t know he was holding and hugged him back.
 
Everyone who had been awkwardly avoiding his gaze and staring at the wall shifted over and joined the hug. So did Wu after some time.
 
Lloyd didn’t cry; he had already cried more than enough. 
 
Still, it was nice to have his family back.

summary: Peace has been restored to Megapolis after the harrowing defeat of the Lady Bone Demon, thanks to the Monkie Kid and his promiscuous friends. With serenity afoot, the demons have fled to the shadows with the idea of Immortals known to the mortal eye. Months have passed, with very little happening and the world at rest, until sudden danger lurks around the corner. Word begins to pick up on the local news of a mysterious substance called "Decay" spreading from island to island off the coast of China—seemingly turning whatever it touches to stone, killing life around it and which, seemingly, cannot be broken, no matter the holy weapon or the power of a vengeful god. Nobody knows of the source of this material, nor does anyone know how to stop the spread of it, causing a tangent of irked fear to fill the public's hearts of the unknown. That is, until one fateful and pouring evening amid April, when a duo of unexpected and unfamiliar faces—a tiny owlet with a deformed wing and a bipedal white feline—stumble into the humble abode of "Pigsy's Noodle Shop," determined to fulfill their quest of stopping the spreading Decay. Arin grabbed his shoulder. “Lloyd? Lloyd, hey, what’s happening—?”

Wukong spent three years running and hiding from Macaque, desperate to avoid being dragged back into the nightmare he barely escaped.
But Macaque refuses to let him go. Before long, Wukong finds himself right back where he started, trapped in the life he swore he'd never return to.

The cruelty and threats that once kept Wukong obedient have been replaced with patience, affection, and an unsettling understanding of everything Wukong longs for. Yet beneath the kindness lies the same need for control. only now it's hidden behind validation, devotion, and the illusion of choice.
Caught between fear, longing, and a desperate desire to be understood, Wukong finds himself slipping back into the very relationship he promised himself he'd never return to.

summary: It's exactly why Wukong isn't surprised when his investigation finds Macaque leant casually against a cliffside stone wall, his elbows rested on the short stack of bricks. No doubt with a cigarette and yep—"Y'know," Macaque starts, the offending cigarette held loosely between two fingers. It reeks, more potent than the incense Master Subhodi used to fill the halls of the monastery with. And that was saying a lot. "Mortals are pretty bad with their films."Well I was expecting more of a 'hello,' but—"I think they do a good enough job," is what he decides on instead. Besides, mortals have always been a creative bunch when it comes to expressing their ideas and emotions. From loud fireworks to puppets cut from the cloth of rice bags, films felt like a long-awaited evolution of story-telling. "I mean, they did make some pretty cool movies about me, so..."A one-shot in which a mortal's documentary problems become an allegory for Shadowpeach.

"How come the legends don't say anything about your staff having, you know—"
"Macaque?" Monkey King goes for a nonchalant shrug but MK can spot the bit of tension there, the stiffness that keeps the movement from being entirely sincere. Still, his mentor continues organizing the shelf in the living room as if nothing's wrong. "Well, for the longest he was just gone from the staff so there wasn't a point to bringing him up."
"What the Great Sage doesn't want to mention is that he killed me," Macaque spits out, floating lazily above MK's head. Despite the bluntness of the statement, there's no anger to it.
"He says you killed him?" MK says, the statement coming off as a question. His eyes look away from Macaque's lazy float at the sound of glass cracking, watching a knickknack crumble to pieces in Monkey King's grip.
"Did he."
It's not a question, it's barely more than an angry exhale of breath, but the mere sound of it sets Macaque cackling just above MK, his tail lightly swiping through the air and smacking the back of MK's head repeatedly.

“Kai…” Cole panted, still stroking as he talked. “G-go easy on him, man. It’s his first time.” Even as he said that, his hands couldn’t help but wander further across Zane’s body, reaching his firm chest and brushing the cold titanium that formed it.
Kai ignored him, wrapping a single wire around his finger and pulling at it. Zane’s throat contracted as the pleasure, so focused on a single, minuscule point, forced out gargled sounds that almost sounded like they’d been choked out of him. “You don’t want that, do you Zane? You don’t want me to go easy on you, right?”
“N-no, please… don’t.” He managed to get out, despite Kai’s increasing pace inside of him. That smug bastard… he was purposely making it as hard as possible for Zane to talk. “This is all so much, I feel like I’m drowning… but I know I can take it.”
-----------------------------------------------------
Zane has been feeling strange since the merge, more sensitive to the world around him. Kai agrees (reluctantly) to help him figure out the cause of this new development, meanwhile Cole watches, supervising the whole thing.

Growing up in a small community on the outskirts of Ninjago City, with no real guidance, no true family and not many friends, you were always behind. Behind your peers, behind your friends, and behind in life. So ultimately, there was nothing special about you.

An elderly couple in the particular town grew fond of you, took you under their wing and treated you as their own child. As you grew up, you became closer to the people in the town, befriending mostly every resident there.
Once you were old enough to work in the city alone, you had applied and got the job to become a waitress/cashier. It was the number one restaurant chain in Ninjago city, Chen's Noodle House.

此版本为《even in death, it’s you》的中文翻译版本。感谢原文作者kr6shout老师授权翻译！译者非专业，会尽力做到“信达雅”，但有翻译的不妥的地方欢迎大家友好指教。此版本仅为同好友好交流，作品全部解释权利归原作者kr6shout老师所有。如果你也喜欢这个故事，欢迎大家在此翻译版本留言，也欢迎大家到原文《even in death, it’s you》下评论夸夸作者！请大家看好tag，此文开头小虐，请酌情观看。若和你的观点不和，请保持理智并退出观看。友好交流，谨言慎行。
以下开始为翻译：-----------------------------------本文为前篇《生生世世皆为你》的续作（如果没读过第一部，有些情节可能感到有些缺失）
敖丙已陨，灵珠未灭。
哪吒的灵魂被失去敖丙的悲痛啃食、掏空。他一路坠入地狱/地府，只为了归还敖丙殒身后却一直藏在自己体内的残魂，为了让敖丙的灵魂安息。但哪吒没有意识到那抹映在他眼底的幽蓝光芒和在心底那始终不肯消散的灵珠气息，其实一直在将他引向敖丙。
在地府，哪吒内心痛彻心扉的呐喊、神魂俱焚的泣诉，却没想到因此唤醒了敖丙的神识，使哪吒竟在掌心重新凝聚出了灵珠。
灵珠重生，天庭震怒恐慌，悟空皱眉；而哪吒怀揣着发着微光的灵珠，一言不发地从幽冥之地走出。他立誓要保护敖丙，绝不会让悲剧重演。
数日之后，当灵珠的外壳彻底修复，一条小小的龙灵自修复完成的灵光中缓缓钻出，轻轻地蜷上哪吒肩头。它沉静、犹豫，带着几分不知所措。
但没错、哪吒不可能认错 - 那就是敖丙。
天庭震怒于灵珠重生，称哪吒此举意为造反，大圣亦觉此事后患无穷。当所有人都将此事视为不祥之兆时，只有哪吒，他把这唤作爱。
无论如何，为了守护敖丙的神魂，又或者，如果能使敖丙真正的归来。
哪吒愿意再次撕裂三界。

title: RISE OF THE ONIDRAGON
author: GreenflameTT_Warrior
summary:
---Takes place during Season 8---
,,From my blood, comes the heir who was promised and his will  be fire and blood..."
,,Darkness is coming with the king and the dead. Only the promised heir can defeat the darkness and bring back the balance which was once stolen while taking what rightfully belongs to his blood..."
"Always remember, Lloyd, we will never be like them. Never. Our way is Fire and Blood..."Words he had always heard from his father and uncle ever since he was little. Words he had forgotten for a while but regained when his father became good again. Ever since then, Lloyd had been training nonstop to gain full control of his true self, while his instincts, his heart, and soul led him to his destined soulmate, who was none other than the fire ninja himself. summary:
The city still glowed white long after the fighting stopped.
MK stumbled through the empty street, one hand pressed tightly against his side as smoke drifted between the buildings. Every step sent pain shooting up his ribs, but stopping felt worse somehow. The silence after battle always did.
His communicator crackled again.
Nothing.
“Cool,” MK muttered weakly. “Awesome. Love that.”
Somewhere in the distance, metal groaned. Neon signs flickered overhead, casting the alleyway in uneven reds and golds. His staff felt heavier than usual in his grip.
He should’ve stayed with the others.
Another sharp pain hit his side and he sucked in a breath through clenched teeth.
Okay. Maybe he was a little more injured than he thought.

summary: Throughout the tales you know and love, MK the Monkie Kid has one that is hard to forget but is well-known. We all know the only reason he became the Monkie kid, was because his mentor, Sun Wukong, was the Great Sage: Equal to Heaven. But what if all that changed? Soren possesses an ancient, terrifying ability tied to gravity, atmospheric force, and compression itself. His powers are so immense that simply existing places crushing strain upon his body, leaving him constantly exhausted and quiet. Every step he takes dents stone. The air grows heavier around him. Most people find his presence intimidating.
But beneath all that pressure is someone gentle, lonely, and deeply caring.
While the other ninja are initially shocked by Soren’s overwhelming strength and eerie calmness, Cole becomes drawn to him almost immediately. As the Elemental Master of Earth, Cole feels an instinctive connection to Soren unlike anything he’s ever experienced — as though the earth itself wants gravity close.

( on break till July) Set shortly after the serpentine era, the story begins when Master Wu brings a mysterious young elemental master to the monastery:
Soren — Lloyd’s long-lost older brother and the rare Elemental Master of Pressure.
Soren possesses an ancient, terrifying ability tied to gravity, atmospheric force, and compression itself. His powers are so immense that simply existing places crushing strain upon his body, leaving him constantly exhausted and quiet. Every step he takes dents stone. The air grows heavier around him. Most people find his presence intimidating.
But beneath all that pressure is someone gentle, lonely, and deeply caring.
While the other ninja are initially shocked by Soren’s overwhelming strength and eerie calmness, Cole becomes drawn to him almost immediately. As the Elemental Master of Earth, Cole feels an instinctive connection to Soren unlike anything he’s ever experienced — as though the earth itself wants gravity close.

summary:
Kai nodded deftly. His head felt like it spun completely around as he did so. “I just want to make you happy,” Kai mumbled. His knees wobbled and gave out, sending Kai crashing to his knees. Sharp pain should’ve registered as shooting through his legs. But Kai couldn’t feel it. He couldn’t feel anything except a heavy heart, dragging him down to the depths.
“Kai!” Lloyd cried out.
Kai ignored Lloyd’s concern. It wasn’t real anyway. None of this could be real. The world he was shown was an illusion designed to lure him in. It was too good to be true. He’d never find a portal to his loved ones inside a lake of monsters. His sister would never understand. Kai could never make Lloyd happy.Years pass since Lloyd and Kai began dating in secret. Lloyd couldn't be happier. Kai on the other hand? Well... He just wants Lloyd to be happy. That's when the merge hits, tearing them apart. Love prevails and brings them together once more. Kai can't lose Lloyd again. But he can't seem to do what's right. He fears Lloyd will never be happy and if Kai can't fix that, neither of them will ever find peace.

He shivered again, hard. Ras needed to do something, since the fire obviously wasn’t enough and his master would be displeased if Lloyd died here.
He reached his paw out, and Lloyd caught it, moving faster than a striking snake. Ras could see the tips of golden claws poking through the ninja’s gloves.
“It’s freezing,” he rumbled. “It’s not like either of us are going anywhere, and you’re a dragon, yes? I am covered in fur.”
“You can not be suggesting what I think you are.”
Ras shrugged. “It is your decision, but it would work best if that gi was not in the way.”
Lloyd dropped Ras’s wrist, tugging at his sleeves. He shivered again, and he let out an annoyed huff. “Fine.” He pushed his hood back, and Ras felt his eyes go wide and his breath stuttered. He clenched his jaw to keep himself from making a sound as Lloyd took off the top part of his gi.

  Oh.
He keeps going, “You’re safe here. You’re safe with Uncle. With MK. With Tang. With all of them. All these years being alone in the dark without a candle to light your way? I can see in the dark, and MK can too now! I’m sure Uncle’s got a match somewhere and all you gotta do is provide the candle.”He scoots closer, taking both your hands now and keeping your gaze. “You. We all are.”○○○After years of running from your past and hiding your scars, you find relief in several wandering destinies that are intertwined with your own. title: Knots and Ties
author: Beancurri
tags: Arin and Sora Don't Know What Romance Is
Lloyd Garmadon Adopts Arin and Sora
summary:
Lloyd Garmadon has never been the best with feelings. Most of the time they're a jumbled mess that he tries to desperately untangle, and he usually fails. When him, Sora, and Arin crash the new Land Bounty while searching for Ras they find something (or should I say someone) that only tightens this knot: Akita, who is undeniably over-joyed to finally see Lloyd again after all these years. She hasn't changed much in appearance, but now that she's not busy plotting the downfall of a tyrannical emperor with control over ice she seems a lot softer.
Arin and Sora haven't really had a problem with feelings like Lloyd's, given that they don't really know what romance is. Is it marriage? Is it some stage in between? When do people stop being friends and become something else? Neither of them know the answer, and as they spend time with Akita and Lloyd they start needing these questions resolved.
But seeing Akita makes Lloyd's head spin, he still doesn't really know how he feels about her, and whether it's stupid to assume she ever really liked him like that. After all the things he's done, would she really like him? His heart hopes so, but his thoughts tell him otherwise.

summary:
This is going to be a huge and ambitious project. I have grown enough to admit to myself that, while Bionicle has absolutely insane, batshit awesome lore and a lot of philosophical potential, Greg Farshtey is just not that good of an author. So... I'll try to make my own. The story will largely stay the same. However, I'll try to fill a bunch of the most egregious plotholes, give some characters who got done dirty by the author a more fitting end, slightly rework the lore to improve the Great Beings and fulfill their potential, oh, and, Screw Greg, LOVE IS CANON!This here is the very first part, a rewrite of Chronicles #1. It will likely stay largely unchanged, apart from a few things to improve the very stilted dialogue and the extremely surface-level relationships and nonexistant character development.
I am not entirely sure how I'll be structuring it though, or how quick/much I can release though.
EDIT: I'll be writing as much as I can get to and add chapters to the existing work as it goes.
Basically, one chapter = one book. Since the books are very short this seems to be the most sensible option for me right now.

“I mean, sure,” Kai pressed on, hoping his voice sounded more reassuring to Jay than it did to him, “your parents can be a little eccentric sometimes, but your mom is totally not crazy.”
“Not my mom.” Jay’s whisper was barely audible, his eyes still wide as his chest shuddered. “My birth mom…”
Kai blinked as his entire world took a sudden, sharp shift on its axis. “Your… what? Jay, what are you talking about? Come on, this isn’t funny.”

Ninjago x thirteen
This book is a sequel to fourteen, where Lloyd went off to school in another realm and got into some messed up teenage shit, and now he's back, and has to help the Ninja investigate a new villain like nothing is different. Obviously, that'll go well.
(A/N has more info)fourteen was kind of like a genderbent version of thirteen set in the Ninjago universe with Lloyd as the doomed teenager, aka Tracy. This kind of happened when I watched thirteen for the first time whilst in the Ninjago fandom. I still love Ninjago and I still haven't seen a male equivalent of thirteen or Mean Girls or that kind of movie in that kind of reckless cathartic teenage way, so I did it myself.
This book can possibly be read without fourteen, but you'll lose a LOT of context, so I'd recommend just settling down for the long run and enjoying the full story

Sora took a step towards him. “I don’t blame you for any of that, Arin. No one does.”
“You should!” Arin shouted. And then, silence. Several moments of agonizing silence. Sora blinked more times than reasonably necessary. Arin looked like he’d just lost a war with his own psyche. Quieter, he whispered, “Maybe I don’t deserve love.”

“Well, well… Someone seems to be struggling to choose where his heart truly lies,” Nadakhan teased with a predator’s grin. “I can help you with that.”
“Na-Na-Nadakhan? Oh no… we weren’t supposed to be alone!” Jay stammered, turning his face away as he threw his arms up defensively.

“Because people disappear when you’re around. Nya’s right over there. I can scream, you know.” Jay snapped, gesturing in her direction.
“Oh, I know,” Nadakhan chuckled darkly. “Well, I guess you’ll keep floundering in that little love dilemma of yours. Nya is a charming young woman, no doubt.” The Djinn’s smile widened, cruel. “But your ghost friend… he has his own appeal, despite being halfway to the afterlife.”

Wu opens his legs and smiles, Morro again stares, mortified, and this time speaks, “Um, I can do it myself Master…It’s ok, I know you’re, uh, busy or-”
“But you like it better when I do it?” Wu frowns. Morro glances at Garmadon, Wu raises an eyebrow and turns to him as well, who offers nothing but a smile, then back to Morro just as confused, as if to say ‘so what?’ And Garmadon again can’t be bothered to hide his amusement, watching the child learn so quickly just how oblivious and unhelpful his master can really be. Morro makes a noise in between a squeak and a groan and relents, kneeling on the floor between Wu’s legs and hands him the comb. Wu hums in satisfaction and pours them their tea.

The Ninja have been suffering since Master Wu's disappearance. With no one to lead them, Lloyd must continue his training to become a Sensei. He becomes more serious and distant. If you told them everything happens for a reason, they would laugh.
You've probably heard it all before. Ivan Garmadon, the adopted child of Garmadon who already had the experiences of a seasoned soldier before they were a teen by the time they had fallen under his care. There, they began to feel normal, yet they didn't have the time to breathe before Fate kicked them out into the streets, now with the responsibility of little Lloyd Garmadon. Stress was changing them, why did they look like this while others looked normal? They could feel the wary eyes everywhere, but they just wanted stability. Someone to care and treat themselves and Lloyd with the love and care they always witnessed other kids experiencing. They quickly learned the world was always going to turn away from the unwanted, and bitterness sprouted in their heart.
Yet when they came to the line, there was an old man there to greet them, and they hated the pitiful looks people gave them. Fate always had a way to play with them.

Long before Time had a name…
You all think you know this story. You’ve heard this opening many times before, preceding the tale of the First Spinjitzu Master and his creation of Ninjago and some of its neighboring realms.
But this is not that story. Elemental Powers, and the world itself, did not begin with that man. There were those who came before him.

Years have passed, uncountable thousands of them, and the Merge brought Change to every land it made of a realm. The beast was vanquished by the knight, a calamity was stopped, and the Shatter Dragon was freed and subsequently destroyed. The Well of Souls was lost in its wake, leaving Departed souls to persist on in the Spectral Lands. Just as they once had when the lands were separate realms.

If he could experience this joy everyday forever, that truly would be his heaven. This closeness they've built, that trust and understanding. Nothing could ever replace or compare to that.
Maybe that's why it was so scary to admit that his feelings towards Geo were changing. That they weren't platonic anymore, maybe haven't been for a long time. To think that he could lose any of this, any part of the relationship they've built — it's scary, unbearable even. He'd never want to make things awkward between them, wouldn't want to force Geo into an uncomfortable situation.

Sus firmas de energía elemental pura, un secreto que los cuatro han cargado desde la infancia y del que desesperadamente buscan liberarse.
El descubrimiento de que Kai puede percibir lo que debería ser invisible lo arrastra a un mundo de misterios y peligros. Pero la verdadera conmoción llega cuando conoce a Nya, la hermana adoptiva de Lloyd
Entre pesadillas recurrentes con mares de fuego y un odio inexplicable hacia el agua, Kai intenta distanciarse del grupo.
Ahora, atrapado entre auras elementales, secretos y un pasado que apenas comienza a vislumbrar, Kai deberá decidir si aceptar su lugar en este mundo de poderes ocultos... o arder en el intento de descubrir la verdad.

“I kept eating, and eating, and eating, until he had holes everywhere on his body. While I ate, he gave up. I’m pretty sure he just had so much adrenaline that he couldn’t feel it anymore. Then I tore his throat out, ripped out his ribcage, and ate his heart right in front of his eyes. He died staring into my eyes. I think it was my dragon side urging me on, but all I felt was triumph.”
 
Morro felt like he was interviewing a psychopathic serial killer. They know what they did was wrong, but they just didn’t care. They had no remorse for what they had done and would have kept doing it. Except, evidently, Lloyd did care. He cared enough to cry genuine tears about it. title: Diaphanous Antithesis (Lloyd Garmadon Robin Au)
author: AsoineMari3
tags: Child Exploitation because let's be honest its there
summary:
In Ninjago City, Lloyd Garmadon lives two lives — one as the son of the city’s greatest villain, Lord Garmadon, and another as its hidden savior, the Green Ninja. But neither identity brings him peace. To the world, he’s a walking reminder of destruction. To his peers, a curse they wish would disappear. Every smile he offers is met with scorn; every act of heroism is overshadowed by the shadow of his father’s name.
Day by day, the walls close in, the weight of expectations, the loneliness of secrecy, and the aching realization that no one truly sees him. Even his mother, kind as she is, cannot shield him from the whispers, the hate, and the exhaustion that come from trying to be light in a city that refuses to forgive his bloodline.
And so one evening, standing at the edge of Ninjago Harbor beneath the eyes of the city that condemned him, Lloyd finally breaks. His voice shakes as he apologizes to a world that never wanted him, and he jumps. The water swallows him whole.

After the chaos of the Tournament of Elements, Master Wu believes the ninja team needs fresh strength, someone with a gift unlike any they've seen. His search leads him to Liora, a quiet, sharp-tongued waitress in Ninjago City struggling to make ends meet and endure an ungrateful home life. Unbeknownst to her, Liora is the Elemental Master of Spirituality, an ancient, nearly forgotten power tied to the soul.
Convinced of her potential, Wu invites her into the world of ninjas and Spinjitzu. But with his own schedule stretched thin, he entrusts her training to the one person who might push her too far: his brother, Sensei Garmadon.
Liora and Garmadon clash instantly. She's impulsive, sarcastic, and unimpressed by his brooding lectures. He's gruff, disciplined, and believes she’s immature and too soft to survive the battlefield. Their training becomes a battleground of wills, full of snark, spiritual power struggles, and suppressed tension.

summary: The robot stood there, blinking around the cell it was in as Garmadon watched from the shadows. Samukai had wanted to tear it to pieces and strip it for parts, but Garmadon had shot that idea down instantly. That mechanic claimed this robot as his ‘son’ and was willing to do anything for it to survive. That was what fathers did. Garmadon knew that well. Who was to say if the mechanic would keep working without proof that the robot was in one piece? If he was as smart as Samukai claimed, then he would ask for proof of ‘life’, if a robot was capable of such a thing.He watched as the robot stared at its own hands like it had never seen such a thing. Maybe it hadn’t. Maybe the skin was new.The robot’s eyes landed on Garmadon and widened. The two stared at each other for a few seconds, the silence of the room deafening. Garmadon blinked and watched as the robot copied it. Slow and hesitant, but it still managed to copy the blink. Garmadon watched as it kept copying his blinks and lifted his left hand. summary:
Weeks after the fall of the Cursed Realm, the ninja believe the story of Morro—the former Master of Wind—is finally over. Once Master Wu’s first and most promising student, Morro became consumed by bitterness after learning he was never destined to be the Green Ninja. His anger led him down a dark path that nearly destroyed everything, including possessing Lloyd and attempting to change destiny itself. But in the end, Morro made one final choice. He returned the Realm Crystal to Master Wu and allowed himself to fall into the Cursed Realm, sacrificing himself to stop the chaos he helped create. Everyone believed he was gone forever. Until the wind brought him back. Reborn in the monastery courtyard with the Realm Crystal at the center of the storm, Morro returns to life at nineteen—short, lean, sharp-tongued, and emotionally distant. Though alive again, he isn’t the same person he once was. Death has left him disconnected, blunt, and unpredictable. The ninja don’t trust him, and Morro makes no effort to earn that trust.

Sometime after the near total collapse of the universe, Wukong and Macaque decided to work on their complicated relationship together. They’d been working together on and off since the Lady Bone Demon’s return, and after having their past thrown in both their faces repeatedly, it felt like it was time to actually address their gripes.

No Use of Y/N for Reader-Insert
summary:
I have always wanted wings, to fly, to breathe. But maybe the process of growing them hurts. For some reason it hurts. Shenxing is stranded in what she recognizes as Lego Monkey Kid, only years in the past, during the events of Journey to the West. Or at least, that was years in the past.
Who are we to wonder where we're going, who am I to tell me who I am.
Xing is overly empathetic, and wants to help. But anytime she tries, the walls are closing in on this mask she's made. She needs to help. If she doesn't help, what is she?
But when, does a comet become a meteor, when does a candle become a blaze.
Stuck in the past and present. Unfortunately, there is no fixing immortality, even if never desired.
When you're falling in a forest, and there's nobody around, do you ever really crash or even make a sound?
She asked for this, until she didn't. She wanted these things, until she remembered she wasn't a fighter. Maybe there were reasons she kept reading. Maybe there was a reason she was drawn into mythology. She doesn't know anymore. Did she even know in the first place?
It's your reflection looking back to pull you down.

Lance Richmond is very good at being watched.
He’s always known how to perform: smile at the right time, joke before things get too serious, act like nothing gets under his skin. It’s easier that way. Easier than being honest, easier than being vulnerable, easier than letting his team see how much he actually cares.

warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
Many knew the story of the Oni and Dragon - mythical beings of destruction and creation, whose clash gave rise to the First Spinjitzu Master. But few have heard of a hidden realm, home to an isolated empire of another mythical creature: the Kitsune. A realm crafted from pure Harmony.
Satomi Kura, a high school senior, sees her world differently. She sees sounds and auras, and dreams of a mysterious figure playing a repeating tune on a shamisen since she was young. But when she encounters a woman her abilities seem to take no effect, her world begins to unravel.
Thrust into the middle of a war, fueled by fractured family ties and forgotten purpose, Satomi must confront her identity, survive battles she never imagined, and stop the looming conflict before it gets too critical. Amidst the chaos, she discovers her lineage - and the powerful destiny that awaits her alongside the protectors of Ninjago.
But underneath it all, something else stirs... something no one is ready to face.

“Do you believe people have the ability to change?” MK inquired, glancing at his closed-off other half.
Crescent stayed silent for a moment. “I dunno,” she admitted. “My Mama did, when he found me. Maybe people just have to choose to change.”
MK considered this. “Do you think we’re gonna change, now that we’ve found each other?”
Crescent glanced back at Mei, eyes lingering for a moment. “I think I already have. Being with you makes me feel complete, and that’s a big change from what I’ve felt before.”
MK’s heart swelled with newfound adoration for his sister. “Same here. Not sure how I survived without you.”
“Tail and all?” Crescent grinned.
“Tail and all.” MK affirmed, and scooted closer to her to lean his head on his sisters shoulder.
Crescent hesitated, but leaned in, intertwining her tails around his right arm. Maybe, even though she had no idea where her Mama went, things would end up being okay.

Newbury isn't just haunted, it's practically a ghost magnet. Luckily, you and your best friends, Jack and Parker, are more than ready to handle it. title: COMPATIBLE - A NINJAGO AU TALE
author: Arachn3rd
summary:
After he gave his life to defeat the Overlord, Zane is mourned as the fallen Titanium Ninja of Ninjago. While the others gather to celebrate his life, Pixal mourns alone in Borg Tower until the unthinkable occurs.
Old recordings come to life. Familiar words resound through the control room. And at the core of the tower, something new begins to build itself.
Zane reenters the world, reborn in titanium, not only with his memories but a new understanding of who he is, who he has become. As he tries to navigate the new joy with Pixal, Zane must fight his own fear that if he presents himself to the other Ninja, will he be expected to be as he was before? And who is Zane now that he has been given a second chance?
While the city goes on without its protectors and the team continues to be divided, Zane must decide whether to return to the light or remain in the darkness until he can figure out who he is.
But before Zane can make that choice, a mysterious new foe attacks, and what ensues is a devastating battle that shatters steel and destroys love in an instant.
Can this new beginning truly be the end?

It was normal, really. Until it wasn't. Having three is unheard of. It's a miracle he didn't die. Or is it a curse? Only time will tell, I suppose.
This world is full of magic. Based on mana levels, a person is either normal or a Conduit. Conduits have high levels of what we call "Sleeping Mana". It means the magic is there, but dormant. How can it be awakened, you ask? Well, it's simple, really. No, that's a lie. It's simple in theory, but you'll probably die when trying to accomplish it. We dragons are very picky, after all.
What, didn't expect to be talking to a dragon? Well, I have news for you, dear reader, you are. My name is Cleo, and the story I'm going to tell you is about me. Well, not really. I'm in it and play a major role, but am not the main focus. That honor belongs to a human.

Jay Walker.

title: "El Imperio Perdido"
author: Monicskyblue
summary: Seis personas. Seis sobrevivientes de experimentos crueles que jamás debieron existir. Científicos jugaron a ser dioses con ellos, moldeando sus cuerpos y despertando poderes que nadie debería poseer… ni soportar. Y aun así, no se convirtieron en monstruos.A pesar de sus habilidades extraordinarias, conservaron algo mucho más difícil de mantener intacto: el corazón. En lugar de buscar venganza o dominar a otros, eligieron protegerse entre ellos. Se volvieron familia. Aprendieron a usar sus dones no para destruir, sino para cuidar a quienes aman. El camino, sin embargo, no ha sido fácil. Han enfrentado persecuciones, pérdidas y decisiones imposibles. Cada paso hacia la libertad parece exigir un sacrificio. Monic, junto a sus amigos, lucha no solo contra quienes los crearon, sino también contra el miedo constante de no saber qué les depara el mañana. Porque sobrevivir fue apenas el comienzo. Ahora deben aprender a vivir.

Gilded Memories Book 5 [SHORT STORY][Wattpad Promote Book 2025]
It's the middle of the night, and everyone is fast asleep. Shops are closed, and the streets are calm, with no loud honks from trucks or cars. Yet, in the quiet of that night, Mk met Milo-a small dog strangely standing in front of Pigsy's Noodle Shop entrance, tongue sticking out and panting as if he had been running around for hours.
"Woah, it's like 2 a.m. Why are you standing here, bud?" the delivery boy asked, crouching down and tilting his head as he stared at the dog, who panted without a care in the world. The little guy seemed happy, too.
Mk couldn't figure out how the small fry ended up in front of the shop's entrance, just standing there as if waiting for him to come out. It was a mystery. However, Milo's sudden appearance in Mk's life turned everything upside down. His deliveries became more adventurous and fun than ever before.
Did Milo follow him back into the shop? Who knows? But one thing is certain-the small pup has become a blessing in Mk's mystical monkey adventures.

The running river in the back calls for him to clean up but he barely wants to.
That desperate feeling, that rush, almost decaying him. It was a primal feeling, natural. Like his teeth longed for the flesh of the green ninja. Not any man or woman, him.

summary: In a world where everyone is born with a soulmate, either romantic or platonic, growing up with colored sight is a rarity. Meeting your soulmate as a child is, after all, a luxury few are afforded — and since touching your soulmate is the only way to break free of the monochrome world every person is born in, most grow up completely colorblind.---Brad Tudabone is the rare exception to this rule. He met his soulmate as a child, touched them, and suddenly, astonishingly, the world was vibrant in color. This would be a great thing, if only it didn't mean he would never know who his soulmate was. Because they were both so young, and separated so soon after, Brad never managed to remember who exactly his soulmate was; all he has is the faint image of vibrant red eyes.---Lloyd Garmadon grew up in a world filled to the brim in color. He tells himself it's because he isn't all human — it's the less painful option. After all, who would want to be the only person in the entire world without a soulmate? The only issue with this white lie, of course, is the faint memory of coffee-colored eyes.

title: The Bitterness of Trying (Haunts Me Through The Night)
author: kaymelondrink
tags: the rest of the ninja are merely mentioned or have one line
summary:
When Sora ran away to the Crossroads, she never expected to find a second family. She never expected to find people who cared for her entire being, whether in the form of her best friend Arin or her newfound mentors, the ninja. Despite all the times she yearned inside to give up, she has shown to them she is a fighter. Independent and resilient, if pessimistic to a fault.
When her past comes to haunt her and unleashes all she had hidden from even herself, how can she tell anyone she is actually a trainwreck waiting to happen?
“It is not wise to bottle up your feelings,” they say when they start to notice the signs. Well, she is not bottling them up. She is simply throwing them up and throwing them away in the cover of the night, a true testament to her ninja skills. That way, nobody is directly burdened with the imperfections little Ana had buried away; nobody will have to tell her to change or hide herself ever again.

“... Not my emperor.” MK grumbles, “Now what am I doing here? Didn’t you say you were going to leave me alone… This isn’t really leaving me alone?”
MK tries to gesture across the room, but his wrists are still banded under the blankets. He finds he can’t move his legs either.
... That ain’t good.
He tries not to think about how this situation is just getting worse.
“Ah,” Azure starts, the darkness in his eyes contrasting with a Mona Lisa smile plastered across his face, “But I’m afraid I am, now.”
Azure leans in, MK leans away.
“And you will listen to me. I will not have a naughty, disobedient cub in my court.”
“Well, good thing I’m not a part of your court.” MK narrows his eyes up at him.
 
He has no idea how wrong he's about to be about that.
..................

The soul is like his magic at times, as fickle as ocean waves at others, and at times, it stings him with the embers of its fires.
 
Everyone carries a piece of themselves within another person. Kei was born from his mother’s soul, from a passionate heart that nearly overflowed with love for him, and from the ghost of a smile shimmering on the horizon of his childhood. Hutchins was another shadow in his life, distinguished from the rest by his moral significance.
 
He is his "father", right?

Not all fathers love their children, and this wasn’t the first time Key had come to realize that.

They say life can change in seconds, but the ninja never believed these words - why should they? Life was constantly changing; there was not such a thing as normal. But what they believed was, that they had finally win this fight.
The Sons of Garmadon were defeated, so like Garmadon himself. Lloyd had his powers back and Master Wu was back to his old self. Great.
It was great, wasn't it? Unfortunately, no one expected what great trouble was coming next.
Evil Garmadon returning and now being in prison was one thing. Little Garmadon, from Wu's childhood days, in the present, a completely different thing.
Just shortly after being bitten by the Great Devourer, the little Lord of Darkness found his way to his family in the future.
To fight the evil inside of him, little Garmadon has to face fate. In the past, present and future.
Can he win this fight?
Who can he believe and trust? And where will his path lead him to? Garmadon doesn't know.

summary: Technically, the lot Brad Tudabone lives on is part of a protected 'dark sky' reserve dedicated to keeping light pollution low and the night sky perfectly visible to the naked human eye. Where he expects to find experimental government technology gone awry, or at the very least an abnormally large rock, he instead finds a futuristic pod holding a living- well. What's the difference between a person and an insect, again? It's the arms, right? Well, this guy has too damn many.___Lloyd Garmadon, ancestor of the First Realm planet and protector of his home planet Ninjago, has no recollection of being stuffed in a cryo-chamber and whisked off into the void of outer space. All he has is a faulty translator and a small database downloaded in his wrist tech. There was an empty, lonesome groan that emanated from the top of the stairs. When they looked up, all of them froze. A figure holding a sword sat perfectly still on an elaborate throne, elevated by about thirty stairs, frozen in ice and snow. The very air around it was so cold that it desublimed right into a solid. A second passed, and the figure opened its eyes slowly, as if waking up from a deep sleep. 
 
It broke itself out of the ice holding it prisoner, tilted its head stutteringly, its neck too stiff. The Ice Emperor silently stepped down the stairs, unperturbed by the stares on his form. He was even more horrifying than her darkest nightmares. This is the man who Lloyd claimed was his friend? This is the man whom both Pixal and E clearly loved? It can’t be. It’s impossible. How could it be?
 
“Who… are you…?” The Ice Emperor growled through a metal mask, brandishing the sword in his hand, which fused with the hilt by the ice. As he got closer, one could see the corrupted crystal overtaking his face, leaving nothing uncovered, and leaving Akita to wonder if the rumors and stories were true. If he really was just a vengeful being made of ice.

Lloyd looked at Zane as though he wanted to argue, but he ultimately shook his head. “But four days is so long! Can't I just look?”
“Give it a rest, Lloyd.” Nya walked into the room, affection practically dripping from her voice as she ruffled her jacket, which was covered in frost. Then, speaking lowly to Zane, “I remember when I was like that. Kai had to safeguard our makeshift tree at night so I wouldn't take a glance!”
Zane laughed at that, the mental image of a little Nya trying to convince her older brother to let her see her presents being tucked away in his mind. He noticed she was in thought. “What brings you out here?”
“Oh! Right, the guys wanted me to get Lloyd. It's snowing!” Nya turned to smile at Lloyd, whose eyes were wide with wonder.
“Snow?” He echoed. “It can snow here?”

summary:
TLDR: You're thrust into a world of powers, mystical beings, and fate that binds people (Will it bind you?). Your name is gone, your existence erased. You start fresh, but at what cost? You may wear the same face and body, but this version of you is a stranger.
What happens if your name is erased? History and social connections rely on names — if people forget yours, who are you to them? The girl they met on Ninth Street? The one with the beautiful smile? Those descriptions don't belong to you; they're for anyone. The only thing that separates you is your name — a name tied to history, intimacy, and substance.
But what if your name was erased? You might think it wouldn't matter, and in some ways, you'd be right.
Now, imagine not just your name, but your entire existence is erased from others' memories. You're no longer part of that world, now existing in another body, in another universe, with no memory of your past. Who were you before?
You’ll have to find out. With a fresh start comes the cost of being forgotten. No one remembers you, no one thinks of you — what’s the point?

Kai's lips trembled very slightly. For a moment, the words knotted in his throat again… but finally, he could speak in a husky voice:"It's been a long time…"His breath cracked."…since I heard that name."____Kai took a deep breath, his lips trembled again but this time he composed himself. "First… no one interrupts," he said. His tone was gentle but carried an "I'm not joking" energy.
Jay immediately raised his hand: "But whaaat—"
Kai raised his eyebrows. "Jay. Please."
Nya crossed her arms. "Say whatever you're going to say, but we're human too, you know, we'll react."
Kai rolled his eyes. "Okay. Then let's agree: I'll tell a piece every day. Either you listen… or you give up."
Silence. The ninjas looked at each other.
Lloyd was the first to give in. "Okay… tell us."____
"This… is where it all begins," he said."It was an autumn day.Winter was approaching…"
Suddenly, the atmosphere changed; with Kai's voice, even the air in the room seemed to cool.
"There was a small village built on a rocky slope, surrounded by dense trees and bushes. This place… was Ignacia."

She sucked in air swiftly, letting it out in pitiful gasps. She was trapped. There was nothing she could do. She couldn’t get enough oxygen in her lungs. The world started to tilt as her vision went blurry. Her shallow breath went in and out, eyes wide as the four walls seemed to close in on her. 
 
Akita was trapped. She was trapped and she couldn’t get out. There was no one to save her and she couldn't save herself. She was alone in a cell, her animal form gone, her travel partners gone, her brother gone. The Ice Emperor sat on his throne, all high and mighty as the Last of the Formlings cowered on the ground. He hesitated a moment before saying, “You know, you can stay here. If you want, of course.”
A low snort. "Is that an invitation, Sparky?"
“Hey, I’m trying to be nice.”
Nya made a skeptical sound, sinking into the softness of his mattress, showing no sign of wanting to move. Her finger absentmindedly traced patterns across his face: his freckles, the pale lines that climbed like roots, the scars beneath the eyepatch. He leaned toward her, closing his eye with a sigh. Perhaps she was also trying to etch this moment into her memory. Just as Jay was drifting off to sleep again, he heard her murmur huskily.
"Don't you dare scare me like that again."
It was too good to be true, he wanted to tease her. There were promises he couldn't keep after all. Instead, he pulled her close and whispered.
“I’ll do the best I can.”

summary:
Some stories skip the ache. Some stories skip the weight. Here, we linger.Kai is barely five when the world he knows shatters. His parents vanish, leaving him to care for his three-year-old sister, Nya, in a house full of shadows and memories. The forge’s roar, Mama’s gentle hands, Nya’s bright laugh—once warm and full of life—now echo only in his memory. Every small task becomes monumental: gathering firewood, feeding his sister, keeping hope alive in a world that has forgotten them. Yet, through trembling hands and fragile victories, a stubborn courage sparks. Each act of care, each flicker of warmth, becomes a quiet promise: they will endure. They will survive. And somehow, they are not lost… because sometimes, even the smallest hands, the littlest embers, can carry the heaviest fires.
I wrote this story because the canon only whispers of what it means to survive when everything familiar is gone. Be gentle with the quiet, and remember: even the faintest spark can light a path through the dark.

summary:
What makes a hero?
MK thought he knew.
A hero, to him, was someone who protected everyone. They put the world before themselves. They're the most selfless, kindhearted people you'll ever meet, saving innocent lives and sparing those that cross them.
But when a new threat rises, MK learns a harsh truth. Not every hero wins the day, and not everyone could be saved. Even the strongest falter, and the brightest lights often cast the darkest shadows.
And yet, not everything is lost. From honing strange new senses to wrangling newborn cubs, MK had grown into his life as a monkey demon, meeting others of his kind and learning their culture. He’s discovered something worth fighting for. These were his people, and this was his home.
But with that discovery comes a harsher lesson. To protect what’s most precious, you must sacrifice your morals. Sometimes, you can’t even protect yourself.
So when clouds gathered over Flower Fruit Mountain, and snow fell far too early, MK knew his world was about to change again.

title: A Frozen Family
author: Anonymous
fandoms: Xi You Ji | Journey to the West - Wu Cheng'en
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
relationships: Liu Er Mihou | Six-eared Macaque/Sun Wukong | Monkey King
summary:
The world had gone still, choked by an ethereal frost that seeped from Lady Bone Demon’s very essence.
But the greatest chill, the most profound devastation, was the one that had settled in the heart of the Monkey King.
His fur, once a vibrant gold, now seemed muted, tinged with the cold, pale light that emanated from his glowing eyes.
Gone was the fiery brilliance, the audacious warmth of his spirit, the mischievous sparkle that had danced within.
In their place, twin pools of glacial blue stared out, stoic and utterly devoid of the playful mischief, the fierce love, or the boundless joy that had defined Sun Wukong.
He was a statue, animated by a force not his own, a puppet with silken strings pulled by the Lady.
And his reward for this ultimate subjugation? The two beings who meant the most to him.

With a shared, mischievous grin, the two monkeys began to grow. Wukong, ever the showman, went first. Golden light erupted from him, swirling and expanding, his form stretching skyward. The mountain beneath him groaned as his limbs thickened into colossal pillars. Soon, he towered over the landscape, a majestic, shimmering giant. Then, with a crackle of energy, two more heads sprouted from his neck, identical to the first, each with glowing golden eyes that scanned the horizon. He let out a booming roar that echoed across the kingdom, a sound that made distant villages tremble.
Macaque’s transformation was quieter, a ripple of darkness. He didn't explode with light, but rather seemed to pull the shadows of the world around him, weaving them into a formidable, powerful form. His fur became like midnight, his six eyes glowed with an eerie purple light, and while he was undoubtedly massive, perhaps only reaching Wukong’s shoulder in height, his frame was lithe, powerful, and utterly devoid of wasted motion. His presence felt like a silent, approaching storm. He looked up at the three-headed Wukong, a small, knowing smirk playing on his giant lips.

“Any last words, Oni?” She asks. The gold so close to his body is weakening him. He won't be able to hold her off for much longer.
“I…think you're really beautiful from this angle.” He says earnestly. If he's going down, he might as well go down telling the truth. He knows she's not going to be dissuaded with much debate. She's far too determined. Maybe he likes that trait in a person. Well, it's not that important now that she's gonna claw his face out.
“Huh?” She asks, in fully genuine confusion. They both stare at each other, blinking slowly. He notices she stopped pushing her claws towards him. He pauses…and immediately pushes her off him, jumping as far as he can. “Okay! See you again! Bye bye!” He calls out, his voice lowering as he gains distance. She groans, adjusting her position. To the forest she goes. Where she lost her brother.

“You heard the man.” Wukong agreed with a stiff smile on his face, untying the creepy smiley guy's ropes. Maybe he should've asked first but he had a feeling Macaque was expecting him to do that, it was like they had a silent communication with eachother. Or well, Wukong hoped he didn't imagine it.

summary:
Shadowpeach Circus AU - Strongman!Wukong x Illusionist!MacaqueThe stage. The applause.
Wukong felt his heart hammering in his chest as he performed. The lights were shining in his eyes and he couldn’t see the faces of the people in the crowd, but he could feel their eyes on him. They were all watching. They were waiting to see his performance. Judging it. He kept on a smile, lifting an iron pole that held a couple of the other performers, bending that pole after lowering them back to the ground, juggling tires with ease and praying he didn’t drop one of them from stress. Did he imagine the way one of them nearly slipped from his hands? He felt like they could all see right through him. They could see that he was struggling to remember his lines. Even though he’d performed this so many times, he still felt like the words were trying to slip from his mind. There were a couple times when he couldn’t even remember the lines that he was supposed to say, but he opened his mouth and they came out anyway. He’d done this performance a hundred times… he could do this. He could do this.

summary:
Shadowpeach Hero/Villain AU“Pspspsps… wakey wakey, Monkey King!”
Wukong huffed a bit at the noise, slowly trying to open his eyes. He quickly gave up, shutting them tightly against the light. Gods, his head was fucking killing him… His knees were really sore… he could feel the fabric of his pants trying to dig into his knees. Trying to bring a hand up to rub his temples, he found his wrists to be tied behind his back. What? Where was he– What was happening??
“Oh, Wuuuuuukoongggg~ I see you waking up. Come on. I believe in you.” That voice came again. Wukong felt his shock turn into irritation as he recognized the voice. He decided to try opening his eyes again. The light didn’t seem to be as bright as he’d first thought. He was interrupted, though, when he felt a strong hit against his shoulder, making him lose his balance and tip over unceremoniously. Morro’s right eye was gouged out of its socket, and his left was cloudy and dull, staring at him with a haunted expression. His Yang Medallion was broken. “Lloyd!” Jay and Nya yelled, seeing their brother on the floor, sobbing as he struggled to breathe. They rushed over to him, one on either side. “Lloyd, what happened!?” Jay said, waving his hands frantically. Lloyd couldn't hear them. When his father was locked away in that staff, it felt like Redson's world became very small. 
He didn't complain. Of course not! He had work to do. Not only did he have to work on freeing his father, he had to learn how to run a kingdom, learn how to dominate in a fight, how to properly behave during a dinner, how to passive-aggressively insult someone to their face, flower language, fan language, sign language, and whatever other language his mother deemed necessary, on top of taking over the multitude of businesses under the Bull family control. There was no time for such nonsense as complaining.
That being said, as he aged into a teen (in demon years), he was forced to learn of the dreadful changes that happen to one's body. He had no choice but to accept it (the increased height and strength were actually quite welcome), yet that didn't mean he had to be happy with it, especially as the subject covered unnecessary topics.

summary:
The Sixteen Realms are home to countless beings. From Mysterium to the Dark Realm, desires differ; from the Departed Realm to the Cloud Kingdom, morality shifts. Yet all are bound by the will of Creation—woven by the First Spinjitzu Master and safeguarded by the Source Dragons.
Beyond these sixteen, no other realms were believed to exist.
But legend tells of four hidden Pillar Realms, the very foundations of creation.
When one of these pillars fell, its people fled in desperation, seeking refuge in the Sixteen. Yet the question lingered: how long can the realms endure if their foundations crumble?
Scientists sought to forge heroes by reshaping life itself, but corruption twisted their efforts. When war engulfed the Pillar Realms, only a handful of scarred yet gifted souls were rescued—spirited away by revolutionaries and cast into the Sixteen as a final hope for survival.
Their destined place of arrival was Ninjago—where some would rise to light, and others would fall into darkness.
Without them, nothing could stop the inevitable.

No matter what happened, fate would bring them back together. She hoped so, at least.
Would they also have a home away from Ninjago like the Walkers? What would happen to the other ninjas? Nya could picture Lloyd older, standing at the head of a dojo, training a new generation of Elemental kids.
Fire, Earth, Ice, Energy, and finally Lightning and Water. There were so many more, she had seen plenty of them back in Chen’s Tournament. Lightning and Water were her favourites though; maybe she was a little biased, who knew.
Jay and her… would they have children? Two of them, maybe with their same powers. A storm, born to continue their legacy. The image made her throat tighten. Would they suffer as much as they have and will?

Wu grinned and slowly tiptoed towards her, using every ounce of ninja training the First Spinjitzu Master had drilled into him. It was only when he was three feet away from her that she lazily opened her eye, staring pointedly at him. “Aww, I’m sorry, did I wake you up?” Wu whispered.
 
Aspheera slowly uncoiled and slithered off the stump, stretching her arms out and deliberately cracking her back. Wu admired the way that the light made her scales shine. “No, I was just waiting, you’re so late today. Is something the matter?” She said, giving him her full attention now that she was done. 
 
“No, nothing’s wrong, I just wanted to give you another gift!” Wu said, excitedly grabbing the staff, and playfully bowing, presenting it to her as if he were a knight and she were a princess. His own electric blue eyes.

It was only visible for a moment. Caught somewhere between a blinding glow and deafening snap, Jordana saw laces of energy unravelling from flesh, lurching and weaving and alive. It was captivating like nothing had ever been before. She wondered what it felt like to wield pure unbridled energy, to live fast-paced and self-assured. There was no hesitation from master nor element. She didn’t even have time to see it claw into Ras’ arm before he and the man were several feet apart, surroundings fading back to their usual sickly green.
And though the lightning had died down, the electricity was still palpable. The man’s hair was still raised like an agitated animal’s, lifted by an invisible charge.
Ras stayed unmoving, but the glint in his eyes exposed his fixation. He would not leave such insolence unpunished.

summary:
Jay looked over his shoulder at the vastness he'd staggered through, lost, his heart racing and his mouth full of blood. He looked back at them, and although the men's expressions were cautious, cold, unchanging, one of their hands slipped subtly into his belt. Jay recognized the gleam of the gun and didn't know why.
"Please, Agent Walker," they asked, but it wasn't a plea, it wasn't a favor. Jay couldn't see their eyes behind their dark glasses. "Don't make this any harder."
This doesn't feel right, was his last thought, the only coherent thread that had been repeated throughout this conversation with these strangers in suits. Jay looked over his shoulder again, overcome by that inexplicable dread, ice in his blood. He didn't know why; he knew he had to run, but he didn't know which way.
So he turned his back on the way he came and followed the agents back into the building.
 
Or: How Jay survives the merge alone, and how he discovers he doesn't have to anymore.

summary:
A mysterious cataclysm has ripped the legendary ninja from their world, leaving their children isolated in the new Monastery of Spinjitzu. What was meant to be a training ground is now a tomb, holding an ancient artifact that is growing more volatile by the day. As the young heroes grapple with their unrefined powers and the immense weight of their new roles, they are forced to confront an uncomfortable truth: the greatest threat isn't coming from outside, but from within the very walls that are meant to protect them.
With their mentors gone, the young elemental masters are left to fend for themselves. Small, chaotic magical disturbances ripple through the monastery, threatening to overwhelm the unprepared team. Every tremor, every flickering light, and every shifting shadow serves as a terrifying reminder that they are alone, left to contain a power they don't understand.
They must learn to rely on each other to face this initial test. As the artifact’s power intensifies, the team’s bonds are forged in the crucible of fear and uncertainty. The line between training and survival blurs, and they realize they are no longer just heirs to a legacy—they are the last defense against an unseen enemy.

Desde entonces, el elemento del fuego no volvió a aparecer en alguien. Se creía que el elemento del fuego fue sacrificado junto a su maestro.
Si existía aún el linaje del último Maestro Elemental del Fuego, hacía ya mucho tiempo que se perdió en el despiadado pasar del tiempo.
Por suerte, las Armas de la Creación daban prestados los poderes elementales a aquellos lo suficientemente fuertes aún sin el elemento apropiado, aunque no tan fuertemente como lo sería con el Maestro Elemental adecuado.

  It was with some consternation that Niú considered his father's head, still proudly mounted in his trophy room over a millennium after he'd torn it from his neck.

  The title of Demon Bull King was one earned by overthrowing, and usually killing, the previous titleholder, and with little exception it was normally a son forcibly taking it from his father. There were rare times a daughter or a grandchild had taken up the mantle instead but generally it was a bloody race between sons.

  Niú had but one child, the Samadhi Fire leaving his beloved unable to provide him with any more, and he could not understand why his only son had not yet tried to claim his birth right. He had been nearly half his age when he had rightly taken what was his!

summary: Sun Wukong was not made for love.Nor for hatred, ambition, or desire.After devouring five gourds filled with elixirs of immortality, his body transcended the limits of flesh—but also the ability to feel as others do. She died betrayed, her crown shattered, her unborn child lost before it ever drew breath.

summary:
Wukong could still remember the first time he’d ever seen all six of Macaque’s ears. The wild orchids were barely starting to sprout in the spring, the air still sharp with the last wisps of winter as they clung desperately to the earth, ultimately defied by the delicate blossoms. The Brotherhood had been formed years ago, but so much time had passed since then it was hard to remember exactly how long it had been. Long enough to start calling themselves brothers, certainly.
He wasn’t even sure how Macaque was even asleep, out cold on the steps that led down into their training courtyard in a horrific position, like he’d fallen asleep halfway through unwrapping his hands, the sheen of sweat already cooled along his brow.
It was the perfect setup for a prank, and who would Wukong be to pass up such an opportunity? He’d probably get punched for it, but who cares, really?
So, he leaned down, pushed the thick mane away from the available…
Wukong froze.

summary:
Listen to my voice, Wukong... only my voice...
Wukong listened. The words were like gentle waves washing away the shore of his thoughts. He could feel his muscles relaxing, the tightness in his shoulders easing. His eyelids felt heavy and comfortable.
Let the sounds outside fade away... let the thoughts inside drift like leaves on a stream...
He felt them go. The buzzing cicada, the arguing clouds, the market noise in his memory – they were floating away, getting smaller and smaller. His mind, seconds ago a roaring ocean, was becoming still.
You don't need to think right now, Wukong... you can just be at peace...

summary: Kai has always tried to be the big brother that Lloyd deserves. Ever since the Green Ninja lost his father, the Fire Ninja has tried to be there for him, to look out for him, and to do everything in his power to protect him no matter the cost. After all these years, he has never once wavered from this strong sense of purpose, which burns brightly like the fire within him. Never once had he faltered, never once had he hesitated to do or give up anything if it meant ensuring his youngest brother’s safety…Except one time.For weeks, that one inexcusable moment of weakness and selfish want has haunted his dreams and tortured him in his waking moments. Never has he been able to forgive himself nor does he feel he ever will be. However, he may find that, after all this time, it was never himself from whom he needed to receive forgiveness. summary:
He knows it isn't Zha'er.
  The voice is the same. The hair, the smirk, the stupid little way he leans back like he owns the sky—same. His ribbon is even tied the way only Hong Hai’er ever got right. But it’s not him. Not really.
  Zha’er never looked at him like that.
  Zha’er burned hot. Quick. He laughed like thunder cracking through heaven and said things he couldn’t take back. He died that way, too—too bright, too fast.
  This one is quiet. Careful. Watching.
  And Hong Hai’er, foolish as he is, plays along. Pretends he doesn’t notice the difference. Because if this isn’t Zha’er…
  Then he’s alone again.
― Zha'er is his best friend. Perhaps even, only friend. So of course he knows the difference between the real Zha'er...and this  fake.

summary:
A flying ship. Lloyd was on a freaking flying ship straight out of a comic book. By all means, this should have been one of the coolest moments in his life. But his mood was dampened by the annoying and stupid inhabitants of said ship. Oh, and they named this awesome ship “The Destiny's Bounty,” which isn’t awful, but Lloyd could have come up with something way cooler. Take, for example,’ Lloyd’s Bringer of Destruction.’ LBD for short. See, now that had a nice ring to it. 
He loved being so high up, watching the people below him, letting the energy of the world mix with the motion of the wind. Inside the ship's walls was too stuffy, cramped with people he didn’t want to see. Out here, he could forget about his kidnappers, and the stupid snakes, and his stupid uncle, whom he didn’t even know existed a few weeks ago.

summary: Be quiet, he commanded internally. His thoughts raged like a hurried torrent, and he was trying to block the stream with a dam made of a handful of twigs. It was that overwhelming feeling when there were so many thoughts it felt like static. He knew that it wouldn’t change no matter how hard he knocked himself round the head like an old TV. Usually he’d blast music in his headphones and draw and sketch the day away, but here, sat in his pyjamas on a city rooftop, he could only watch the sun rise higher.He shifted on the ledge, feeling his backside going numb on the bricks he was perched on, “You’d think the sunrise after an attempted murder would be more exciting or something.” He muttered, blinking his eyes sleepily, then he squinted, “huh, although, by saying that I’ve probably jinxed—“A loud scream echoed around the streets.“Damn, I hate plot convenience.”ORAfter the events of Season 4, MK’s left fumbling for control. While his new monkey form worked great against Azure, well… let’s just say that it didn’t want to be bottled back up again. "Handful of Topaz" is one of those tales, for example.I thought I would provide an anthology of short tales, character perspectives, and deleted scenes. summary: Every month, the Ninjago Fandom Wiki runs a Writing Contest based on a simple prompt. Since June of 2024, I've participated multiple times, and even when I haven't officially written or entered, I've at least come up with some idea or another.This is a collection of those contest entries. Many of them are one-shots, some slightly longer, but mostly just little vignettes that could easily fit within Ninjago's canon. He walked towards the center of the courtyard, sitting cross legged on the ground. His breathing hitched as he fought for composure, tears pricking the corners of his eyes as his vision blurred. Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, king of the monkeys, sat atop his favorite peak, not with his usual confident swagger, but with slumped shoulders and a furrowed brow. summary:
Lloyd looked up at the night sky from the roof he was patrolling on. The few stars he could see glittered lonely, far away from each other. The light of the city obscured theirs, a sad sight, really.
The loneliness of the stars reminded him of his own isolation. He had spent his whole life wishing for people to support him (beside his mom and uncle, of course). A teenager now, he didn't think he could bring himself to hope anymore.
Sometimes though, when he looked at the sky, if he was lucky enough to catch a shooting star, he could almost hear the wish being whispered in the back of his mind.
Shaking his head, he looked back up on last time, spotting what he thought might be small meteor headed right down toward the city, tinged a light green.

summary:
Ever since he was a young Serpentine, Frak had always done his best to be brave.
 
It wasn’t always easy, like how since he was one of the only Serpentine in a school otherwise full of humans, he’d sometimes catch wind of a less than nice comment about his species, either from his own classmates or their parents. Or the fact that he was a loud and proud Ninja fan, which, while it was very common to be a fan of Ninjago’s heroes, being a geek about it like he was was very much deemed uncool in the eyes of his peers.
 
But Frak’s parents, lawyers and activists for Serpentine rights, taught him to take pride in his heritage and identity. And the Ninja, especially Master Cole Brookstone, his favourite Ninja ever, taught him to stand up to all those cruel and unjust.

She had rushed to the scene despite her co-worker’s insistence not to. The ambulance was there before she was, and she saw the blood on the ground as paramedics loaded you up into a stretcher.She pushed past officers and doctors alike, still in her nightgown. The officers there tried to stop her from reaching you, but she pushed past with the strength of a mother. She peeled back the material hiding your face from view, and sobbed at the sight that greeted her. Your eyes were open, empty and lifeless, and dried blood spilled down your mouth. Warm blood was still slowly oozing out of your neck.

But just because society has moved one doesn't mean elemental powers and such believes aren't still being pass down to each new generation.
Elemental masters are typically depicted as protectors or heroes, it runs in their blood. Now that the world has ceased to believe the existence of the very elemental masters that used to protect their ancestors, Cole and many other elemental master have opted to keep their inheritance to themselves.
Not only does the will to bring justice upon people runs in his blood. But something much deeper and meaningful had pushed Cole to apply to his duties, he made a promise to himself to continue his mom's legacy and dreams. summary: Los ciclos iban a acabarse. Nüwa no podría seguir aguantando los ciclos y la barrera por más tiempo.Sin embargo, en lo más profundo de su desesperación, una esperanza brilló en el mundo. Pero seguía siendo su creación y Nüwa amaba sus creaciones. Así que sabiendo que podía sobrevivir en el mar del caos, lanzó la estrella con todas fuerzas, esperando que encontrara otro mundo en el que pudiera ser feliz.
