summary: Fighting with Wukong is habit for Nezha. A game, almost, especially on the "Great Sage's" side, him being typically the one to initiate it, whether by wreaking havoc in the Celestial Realm or simply swiping his tail under Nezha's legs to trip him up, smug grin constantly in place. Wukong grates on him in a way he used to wish his brothers would—in a way he'd seen many other brothers conflict, a push and pull, tumble and scrape that looked so much more intimate than the cool reserve Nezha had with his own blood.There had been something cathartic to it. Something... fun. Nezha had never felt much real bitterness or fear; alarm, yes, distrust certainly, and incredulity—a frantic sort of disbelief that Wukong would be so cocky and so foolish, as when he took the scroll to the Samadi fire, but—not true fear.Not the terror and despair choking his throat as he feels now..In a world where Sun Wukong joins the Brotherhood in a rebellion against the Jade Emperor, Nezha faces impossible odds trying to stand his ground. Or: the one where Nezha stands basically alone against the rebellion, is promptly bodied, and then picked back up.

What would you do with a drunken sailor
summary:
Myths surrounded the uncharted island to the west. It was said to hold a magic treasure, but sailors who tried to claim it rarely made it back. Those who did return spoke of a haunting song that lured them in, only to be followed by a violent storm. No accounts existed of anyone who had reached the shore and lived to tell the tale. The island's man-eating guardian rises from the depths to slaughter those who survive.
With nothing left to lose, Sun Wukong took on the challenge, but quickly failed. He found himself shipwrecked, and he realized that someone saved his life. Little did he know, his savior was not what he seemed.
When the Pirate King woke up, he came face-to-face with the source of the singing, a siren unlike any other. The guardian of the island, Tidesinger, whose real name was Macaque, was sharp-tongued and wickedly beautiful.
At first, it was a game of survival. Wukong flirted like his life depended on it, while Macaque decided whether this foolish pirate was worth the trouble of keeping alive.
But things soon turned into something far more dangerous. As Wukong unveiled the siren’s secrets, he realized he wasn’t just fighting for his own life, but for Macaque’s, too.

Macaque had come back to life irrevocably changed in many ways and his apparent impotency had probably been the least of his worries considering everything else that had happened. But it had certainly been a cause for some stress as they had tentatively taken steps to deepen the physical intimacy between them.

The first time the Red-Bottomed Horse Monkey opened her eyes it was to cries of distress.

  But for a long moment, all she could do was lay there, dazed, as she tried to make sense of her new existence and the near perfect white void that she had awoken to.

  Qì, her mind provided.

What the brotherhood wanted to do those hundreds of thousands of years ago. Of course, the big question most people would have to hearing such news is what are you going to do differently? What makes you better than the man who hate so much? That is what Azure sets out to do. To finally after all these years help others. Then you have Mk. Someone who still in his youth became something he never thought he would be. A hero. One trained by his own hero Sun Wukong. And he loved it. But when Azure took him away, locked him in that scroll, and sliced it in half he couldn’t help but fall into despair and couldn’t stop the brotherhood from striking down the emperor. “We aren’t strong enough to stop him” Mk said. It a sad truth that the rest of his friends accept. Though not all is lost. For Buddha decides to help Mk to realize his full potential, to find a way to save Wukong and take down the brotherhood

summary: The Sun is always a strong figure, a powerful hand, a worthy provider. When people are asked to picture or visualize the sun they think of a strong figurehead with perfect everything. The sun was something special, it gave life to a single planet in the solar system and supplied the light for the moon to get attention as well. But even so, in the end, a sun is a star. Stars will experience supernovae but if they are small enough this doesn’t happen and they just expand and burn out, dying in that way as well. A burst, that spreads out the matter. It’s an explosion, and even before, there are always signs that that star is burning out, the dimming of its lights, the deteriorating of its physical state. Of course, nobody notices because there are thousands of stars in the sky. But when the sun does it, it's something people try to ignore or brush under the rug. It's hard thinking about the thing you rely on for your life… is just as fragile as you are.

summary:
“MK!” Mei shouts again. Her voice started to scratch. “MK!” She held an arm up over her face to protect from the elements, but it only did so much. The wind fought against her every step, her hair loose and whipping around, blinding her
Every flash of lightning she noticed more about the disarray of the ship
The first flash showed that the sails were ripped.
The next showed the mast was in two, with one piece slamming into the deck with a crack
The third revealed a man on the ground, still, unmoving
If he wasn’t dead yet, he’d certainly be soon
“MK!” She shouted again, voice hoarse and desperate
Someone grabs her arm. Instinctively she shouts and pulls away, shoving the stranger and stumbling back
“Mei! It’s just me!” They shout; despite only being a few feet away, Mei still has to strain to hear
“Oh thank God!” She jumps back forward, pulling him into a hug
But it only lasts a moment, until Mei pulls away, shoving the jacket into his arms. “Put this on!” She commands, grabbing MK’s arm and yanking him forward as he stumbles, slipping on the other sleeve.
“What are we going to do?”

MK appraised the giant, decrepit house in front of him and found himself underwhelmed, "You dragged me out of bed for this? A haunted house? Really?"

  Mei threw an arm around his shoulder and poked his face, "Oh, don't be such a party pooper! This place is the real deal - kids online have been saying they heard and saw all sorts of things in there! And it's got a classic haunted house backstory to go with it! C'mon - look at this place and tell me it doesn't look the part!"

  It was actually almost comical how perfectly the place looked the part. It was practically textbook in its appearance - boarded up windows, damaged roof, dead trees - it had it all.

  He pointed to his eyes, "I literally have Golden Vision - I could use it right now and find out what this places deal is."

  Mei grinned as she pulled out a matching pair of bracelets, "And that's why I swiped these bad boys from the vault."
Ruh-roh.

Quickly I turned into an alley way for a faster shortcut. My now muddy shoes steadily splash through questionable colored puddles. An in my rush I almost did not hear the high pitch cry from the brick wall I ran buy. This sudden sound caused me to stop in my tracks. Look Back. And see The form of a little boy no older then 2. He stared up at me with his big eyes full of water that I bet weren't from the rain. My world felt like it stopped, and I ignored the feeling of my hair growing heavy from the rain water. The little boy also stopped crying and just kept staring with those eyes I could not place words to describe. Quickly I came over and kneeled down and took off my rain jacket to cover his unclothed figure. "Hey their you... you- um little Goober! But anytime it'd get remotely close to her, she'd awake in a cold sweat. Who or what was that thing, and why was it stalking her in her dreams?

title: Power Exhaustion
author: Spookybee03201
tags: you can pry that season out of my cold dead hands
summary: Nezha is no stranger to being tired. He works constantly, remaining vigilant at almost all times. He goes days without sleeping frequently, even though, as a God who was once a human, he needs only slightly less than a human would. He knows what it feels like to overuse his powers and need a break, because of course he does, it comes with his job, but this is different.The Jade Emperor’s power is massive, a writhing ball of pure energy, dense and thick and heavy, and not just in weight. Holding it in a seal like Nezha’s is incredibly taxing, and it would be to someone more powerful than him, too.But he bears it as best he can, isolating himself to do it. He must be awake and alert, focused solely on the task at hand for things to remain under control.-----Day 10 - Lego Monkie Kid - Nezha - Power Exhaustion

If you asked Macaque before the incident why he followed The Monkey King, he would tell you he would go to the ends of the universe for him. If you asked him now, he would be terrified even to say he understood Sun Wukong. They were always together. They always stood by each other. But after that fateful day, a day filled with uncontrollable rage and death, Macaque was terrified to be on the other end of the staff. Especially if Wukong was the one holding it. After Macaque’s return, he hid amongst the shadows of Flower Fruit Mountain, only to discover that two new stone eggs were placed upon the highest point. Sun Wukong would return occasionally, never giving the stone eggs any thought. Macaque did everything he could to care for them, knowing what was beyond the stone shell. They drew energy from Macaque, and occasionally a ton from Wukong.

summary:
Jay was avoiding him. Cole wanted to shake him and ask why, why he was pulling away.
  “Was it something I said? Jay, I’m sorry. We said we wouldn’t be awkward anymore. Please talk to me.”

  
    He sighed. Maybe Jay had figured out his crush. Maybe he hated him now.
  

  
    He’d been so stupid, thinking that he’d had a chance when Jay asked if he had a crush. Maybe Jay didn’t like him, even as just a friend — who knew? Jay was being all secretive and pulling away, probably because of something Cole had said.
  

  
    And now everything with Jay was awkward again.
  

  
    Things weren’t supposed to be awkward anymore.
  

  
    ~
  

  
    Six years ago, Jay and Cole became best friends. Two years ago, they fell out out touch. Four months ago, they found each other again. They should be best friends, the inseparable duo.
  

  
    So why aren't they?

Then the ugly, snaking line cut through the angry mess, covering it and mostly hiding the words’ meaning.The mess was ugly, but at least there was that nice, little smiley face. Looking at the round, happy face, he could almost forget that the inky splotch blob was there.“Dinner should be ready in fifteen minutes. Are you done with your journaling, Lloyd?” Wu asked, casting his young nephew a glace as the old Spinjitsu master steadily balanced four different bowls of steaming food on various parts of his body.Lloyd blew on the damp ink, then closed his new notebook. “Yes, Uncle Wu. I’ll put this away, then I’ll be ready for dinner.”---Post Lego Ninjago movie. Lloyd has a hard time, gets sick, shares wholesome (and occasionally difficult) moments with family and friends, and to top it all off his mom says that his genetics might be trying to "express themselves." summary:
Another thud sounds, this time with its own hum of displeased chatter.
  MK sighs. Just as he thought.
  The dull rumble of Monkey Kings voice intermingles with Macaque's high-pitched tone, their bitter symphony an unintelligible echo through the bedroom door.
  Despite his presence the barking continues, bits of the conversation filtering through the closed door.
  
    "And if...you..."
  
  He takes a step forward.
  
    "...look, just..."
  
  Another.
  
    "...the others don't...!"
  
  MK finally presses his ear against the cold wood.
MK expected a lot of things when Peng showed up an inch away from death on Monkey King's doorstep. An attack from whatever hurt the eagle. Arguments from the group about what to do.What he didn't expect was for Macaque to be so aggressive about leaving Peng to fend for himself. There's history here. History MK is determined to discover.

summary:
“Brainy kid to rescue,” he declares. “I found a couple of, uh, well- old bowls!"
  MK’s head lifts triumphantly, prepared for the resounding “-good job, kid/bud” © that both Macaque and Monkey King had gotten into the habit of offering.
  But silence only greets him, MK cracking an eye open to make sure Macaque hadn’t abandoned him.
  The shadow is right where MK remembers, almost eerily still. The only notable difference is the sudden roundness of Macaque’s eyes and the subtle childish spark of something that lurks there. If Mk didn’t know any better, he would’ve called it fear.
  
    “Macaque-?”
  
  
    “Where did you get those.”
  
After getting his ass kicked in a sparring match, Macaque sends MK to fetch some bowls from the dojo's kitchen. Only problem? The only bowls MK's able to find resemble more of a failed art project than a bowl. One resides more smooth and refined, the other far more clumsily made but with small engraved peaches and a fingerprint on its side.Huh, that's kind of cute. Surely picking these bowls won't lead to bodily harm.

summary: Macaque.The very thought of him made something coil tight within Wukong’s chest. Despite their uneasy alliance, the tension between them had settled into something…more palpable. He had agreed to trust MK’s judgment about the dark-furred monkey, but there were times when Macaque’s gaze felt like a physical thing—like it reached through him, clawing at something he didn’t want to acknowledge.That gaze. The way the shadow monkey’s eyes seemed to gleam with something darker, something deeper, left a chill crawling up Wukong’s spine. There was a hunger there. Hungry for what? He wasn’t sure.Wukong tried to ignore it. It didn’t matter. Whatever Macaque wanted from him, it wasn’t worth his time. He was used to dealing with threats, both subtle and overt.What he didn’t know, however, was that Macaque’s gaze (always so unsettling) wasn’t just a passing thing.It was the beginning.The beginning of something that would consume him entirely.

“I’m forgetting Jay.”
  
  
    Those weren’t the words she had intended to say.
  
  
    She wasn’t forgetting him, she knows what he looks like, knows what his laugh sounds like, knows what his favourite foods are.
  
  
    She knows Jay.
